messages:
mira: heads-up — canary for model v4.2.1 went live at 09:12. p99 for text-gen route shot up ~2.6x within 30m, not constant but repeated spikes.

alex: saw CI alert too: perf/regression flagged p99 +150% on batch=8 synthetic. CI points at the model metadata tokenization bump in PR #3421.

ricardo: grabbed a flame graph from a canary node. heavy stack in runtime::alloc_hotpath and kvcache::insert, repeated small allocations during KV warmup.

zane: interesting — the v4.2.1 change was a tokenizer normalization tweak that inserts a zero-width marker for a subset of locales. That could change token splits and thus sequence-length distribution.

alex: I pulled pre/post histograms. before: majority seqs <= 64. after: significant mass moved into 65-180 range. kernel-selector is picking different kernels for the longer tail and we're seeing fallback oscillation when batch aligns change.

ricardo: allocator traces show many ephemeral KV keys because the prefix used for kvcache differs (leading marker sometimes present). so keys that used to hit now create new entries then get evicted -> lock contention.

mira: CI bot posted the job: 
```text
ci-bot: perf/regression v4.2.1 batch=8 p99 baseline 160ms -> 416ms
notes: runtime allocator hotlock, kvcache churn, kernel-fallback spikes
```

ci-bot: auto-bisect running; narrowed commits to tokenizer normalizer + model-metadata stamp between hashes 9a3f2..9a3f8.

zane: local repro command: `./bench --model v4.2.1 --seq-profile mixed_tail --batch 8 --iter 300` reproduces p99 jumps. sharing minimal output.

alex: quick mitigation idea: bias kernel selector to a stable kernel for seq<=192 with a small traffic percentage to reduce oscillation. opened runtime/selector-guard PR.

ricardo: also tried toggling normalize_kv_keys=true at runtime on a dev node; that removed alloc explosions and p99 returned near baseline. suggests key normalization mismatch is main vector.

mira: plan proposal: 1) pause canary, merge selector-guard as short-term mitigation; 2) fast rollback of tokenizer normalization if needed; 3) add CI regression test covering tokenization variants.

alex: selector-guard on 10% showed p99 drop ~25% in a short window but throughput down ~3%. deploy-bot paused canary at 12% because latency alert triggered.

ricardo: adding temporary metric `kvcache_prefix_variants` and increasing heap-sample rate for canary nodes to capture more stacks.

mira: if selector-guard doesn't stabilize within 45m we flip rollback. alex please keep the rollback PR ready (rollback/3421).

ci-bot: queued perf job for selector-guard PR.

zane: note for postmortem: tokenizer changes that affect token boundaries can have outsized impact on batching heuristics and kernel routes; we should treat tokenization shifts as a perf-sensitive change and require perf smoke before model onboard merges.

mira: agree. also add a small unit that simulates leading-marker variants in CI tokenization tests. ricardo, can you paste the allocator histogram you captured?

ricardo: pasted histogram snippet:
- allocs/sec pre: 1.2k -> post: 5.8k (peaks aligned with seq-tail requests)
- lock contention ms: 0.3 -> 12.6
- kvcache miss-rate for popular prefixes: 0.04 -> 0.31

mira: thanks everyone. keep this thread updated. if selector-guard stabilizes we can continue canary ramp, otherwise we'll roll back tokenizer normalization and re-onboard with a compatibility layer for KV keys. :mag:
